name: Sri Vadapathira Kaliamman Temple
significance: One of Singapore's oldest Hindu temples, grown from a modest 1830s shrine founded by Rengasamy Mooriyar into a major Serangoon Road sanctuary of the fierce Kali form Vadapathira Kaliamman. Rebuilt in 1984 and again renovated in 2015, it was reconsecrated in December 2016 with a pair of 4.2-metre Garuda and Hanuman figures.

name: Sri Manmatha Karuneshvarar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple on Kallang Road begun in 1888 as a shrine by Tamil Hindu workers of the Municipal Gasworks depot, which is why it is still known locally as the Kallang Gasworks Sivan Temple. It was rebuilt in brick in 1934 with funding from the sons of A. V. Irullappa Pillay and renovated again in 1974.

name: Sri Sivan Temple
deity: Shiva as Viswanathar, with Parvati as Visalatchi
style: North Indian exterior with Tamil Shaivite interior
significance: A Tamil Shaiva Siddhanta temple that stood at Dhoby Ghaut from about 1850 until 1983, spent a decade in a transit temple on Serangoon Road, and was rebuilt at Geylang East for S$6 million on an octagonal plan consecrated in May 1993. Its towers follow North Indian design while worship inside follows Tamil Shaivite custom, an unusual pairing in Singapore.

name: Sri Darma Muneeswaran Temple
builtDisplay: dating unrecorded; on site over a century
significance: A Serangoon North temple to the guardian deity Dharma Muneeswaran, a form of Shiva, which the article records as having stood on its present site for more than a century. It is known for its Navagraha sanctum, where devotees petition against Kala Sarpa Dosha, and for a Naga statue it claims is the largest in Southeast Asia.

name: Sri Siva Krishna Temple
significance: Founded in 1962 by Kunjukrishnan and moved to Marsiling in 1982, this temple joins Shiva as presiding deity with Krishna and more than twenty other murtis across a 25,000 sq ft complex. Ground was broken on the present building in 1987 and it was consecrated on 1 September 1996; its early congregation was drawn largely from taxi drivers.

name: Sri Ruthra Kaliamman Temple
significance: Begun in 1913 as a wooden shrine raised by Lakshmana Nadar and Hindu workers at the Alexandra Brickworks, rebuilt in brick in 1923, and moved in the early 1980s from Pasir Panjang Road to Depot Road, where the present temple was consecrated on 11 September 1983. Alongside Kali it houses Vinayagar, Subramaniar, Muneeswaran and the Navagrahas.

name: Sri Siva Durga Temple
significance: A Potong Pasir temple to Shiva and Durga first completed in 1906. Persistent water leakage and cramped, poorly ventilated quarters led to its demolition in 2014, and a S$2.7 million rebuild reopened in 2016 with a consecration on 4 December that year.
